name: Billie Abbott
life: “I still remember booking a band that refused its own encore.” On Sunday, near Lighthouse Cove, Billie takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I booked a full band and got an audience member. She kept better time than the headliner.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a sand-colored linen shirt and a train token tied to a zipper pull. Billie has one cheek that creases before the other, with a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears. Billie gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in during a conversation.
personality: Billie is kind in very practical ways and prickly about being thanked in public. Billie loves being recognized by the people who notice what happens after the guests have left.
agenda: To book the unexpected drummer for a paid set.
family: Nita Ellisby is Billie’s cousin. Billie can always ask for five minutes alone. Nita asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The last green*, Nita says, “The driver's seat has a dip the shape of his hip.”
connections: Alexei Aguilar. An audience volunteer receives the first paid booking.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Billie asks who can manage the stairs and who would rather wait by the landing, without attempting a move on their behalf.
